app.name: MalariaX
app.tagline: Know your risk. Protect your community.

common.offlineBody: Your answer is ready and your report will upload when you reconnect.

home.subtitle: Are you or someone you know unwell? Start here.
home.checkSelfBody: Answer a few questions about fever, chills and how you feel.
home.checkAreaBody: See the malaria risk where you live, right now.
home.askQuestionBody: Prevention, symptoms and treatment, in your language.
home.reportCaseBody: Help your community by sharing what is happening locally.

assess.title: Symptom check
assess.subtitle: Tick what applies. This takes about a minute.
assess.childNote: Children who are unwell need to be seen quickly. Answer carefully and read the warning signs on the result.
assess.dangerNote: Any of these needs same-day care, not tomorrow.
assess.regionWhy: Your region is used to check local weather and reported cases. It is never linked to your name.
assess.ageLabel: How long have these symptoms lasted?
assess.soughtCare: Have you been to a health center for this?

result.title: Your result
result.watchBody: If any of these appear, go to a health center straight away.
result.disclaimer: This is not a medical diagnosis. Malaria can only be confirmed with a blood test at a health center. If you are worried, get tested.
result.emergencyBanner: Go to a health center now. Do not wait.
result.offlineNotice: You are offline, so this result uses the built-in clinical rules only. Reconnect for a fuller explanation.

low.label: Low risk
low.headline: Keep watching, and keep using your bed net.
actions: Sleep under a treated bed net every night, including during the day.
Drink plenty of clean water and rest.
Check again tomorrow if the fever does not settle.

moderate.label: Moderate risk
moderate.headline: Please get this checked at a health center.
actions: Visit a health center for a rapid diagnostic test or blood test.
If you are given medicine, finish the whole course even if you feel better.
Keep sleeping under a bed net, and avoid mosquito bites during the day.

high.label: High risk
high.headline: Go to a health center today.
actions: Go today, and take someone with you if you can.
Write down when the fever started and any medicine you took.
Ask for a blood test. Do not rely on fever alone to decide.

emergency.label: Emergency
emergency.headline: Go to a health center now. Do not wait.
actions: Go to the nearest health center or hospital immediately.
Take someone with you, and do not travel alone.
Ask a health worker, or call 991 if you cannot travel.

redFlags: Vomiting again and again, or unable to keep fluids down
Confusion, unusual behaviour, or difficulty staying awake
Very dark urine, or yellow eyes and skin
Bleeding, or feeling too weak to stand

report.title: Report a case
report.subtitle: Reports are anonymous and help your area get prepared.
report.zonePlaceholder: Optional — add if you know it
report.duration: How long has this person been unwell?
report.privacyBody: Reports have no name, phone number or exact location. We only keep the region so we can spot areas that need help.
report.consent: I understand this report is anonymous and is used for public-health planning.
report.success: Thank you. Your report was sent.
report.successQueued: Saved. It will send when you are back online.

dashboard.title: Malaria risk map
dashboard.subtitle: Reported cases and weather, by region.

provenance.estimated: Estimated from weather and altitude. No case reports yet.
provenance.live: Based on current weather for this region.

dashboard.noData: Not enough reports yet in this region
dashboard.noDataBody: Risk will appear here once people report from this area.
dashboard.notConfiguredBody: This build has no database attached, so regional risk cannot load. Everything else — symptom checks, prevention advice and offline reporting — still works.
dashboard.suppressedBody: Showing this number could identify the people who reported, so we hold it back until there are at least five.
dashboard.driverRain: Rainfall above the seasonal average creates standing water for mosquitoes.
dashboard.driverTemp: Temperatures in this range let the malaria parasite mature quickly.
dashboard.driverHeat: Very high temperatures shorten mosquito development time.
dashboard.driverDry: Hot, dry conditions reduce mosquito breeding.
dashboard.driverCases: A high number of cases has been reported here recently.
dashboard.prepNets: Check every bed net for holes and repair or replace them.
dashboard.prepDrain: Empty pots, tyres and water tanks at least once a week.
dashboard.prepKnow: Know the name and location of your nearest health center.
dashboard.prepDays: Use repellent during the day — mosquitoes also bite in daylight.

season.peakBody: Most malaria transmission happens right now. Prevention matters most in these months.
season.buildingBody: Risk is rising as rains begin. Prepare now before cases increase.
season.decliningBody: Risk is falling, but stay protected until the season ends.
season.lowBody: Fewer cases now. Use this time to repair nets and clear breeding sites.

bring: Any medicine or a packet you have already taken
A phone, so the clinic can call you
Someone to go with you, and a way to pay for transport
Note the day the fever started
care.sayBody: Say when the fever started, whether you have vomited, and whether you have used any medicine. This is the information they need to test and treat you correctly.
care.localBody: Ask someone nearby — a health extension worker, a pharmacy, or your kebele office — which health center is closest and whether it has a malaria test. Most health posts can do a rapid test on the spot.
care.urgentOnly: Show this only for high or emergency results
